Thanks for reaching out! Team event scoring usually works by tracking specific actions you complete during the event window, and those points are added to your team's total—but only actions that match the event's listed criteria count. If your points aren't showing up, a common reason is that the action taken doesn't match what the current event is tracking, or it happened outside the event's active time window.

Check the event details screen in-game (usually accessible from the event banner) for the exact scoring rules and eligible actions for this specific event, since these can change between events.

Hey! The exact start date for the next season usually gets announced in the in-game news or announcements section shortly before it goes live, so that's the best place to check for the official schedule. Some games also post this info on their official social media channels or community forums—worth a look there too if you want early word. If you're not seeing anything yet, it likely just hasn't been announced. Keep an eye on the game's main menu or news tab for the update!

Great question! Pets usually give you passive bonuses or special abilities while they're active — things like boosting resources, helping in battles, or unlocking extra actions. The exact effect depends on which pet you unlocked, so check its info or details page in-game (usually a tap-and-hold or info icon on the pet itself) to see what it specifically does and how to level it up or activate its ability. That'll give you the clearest picture of how it fits into your strategy.

Hey there! Team codes are usually entered from the Team or Guild menu — look for an "Join Team" or "Enter Code" button, sometimes tucked under a "Search" or "Invite" tab depending on the version you're on. If your friend already created a team, they should be able to send you a direct invite instead of a code, which might be easier to find under your Friends list or notifications. If you still don't see any of these options, check that your game is updated to the latest version, since older versions sometimes hide or move that menu.

Hi there — the max village level depends on which game/version you're playing, since caps get raised with updates. The best way to check is to look at your Town Hall or Village upgrade screen in-game — it'll show the current highest level available along with what's needed to reach it. Patch notes or the official game website usually list this too if there's been a recent cap increase.

Yes, there are usually a few ways to earn spins without spending money. Check the game's news/announcements section, official social media pages, and any in-game daily rewards or challenges — free spin links are often posted there and can expire fast, so use them soon after you get them. Also check the game's official website or community forum, since that's where these links are usually shared. If your friend can send you the exact link, you can try it directly in the app to see if it still works.

Good question—shields typically work differently depending on the type your game offers. Usually a shield protects your base from being attacked or raided while it's active, but some games have separate shields for PvP raids versus resource attacks, or exclude certain actions like scouting. The best way to be sure is to check the shield's description in your item inventory or the help/info section in-game, since it should list exactly what it blocks and for how long. If there are multiple shield types available, comparing their descriptions side by side should clear up the disagreement with your team.

The daily bonus reset is based on server time, not your local time zone, so the exact clock time will vary depending on where you are relative to the server. To check when yours resets, look at the countdown timer shown on the daily bonus screen in-game—that will tell you exactly how much time is left until the next reset for your account. It won't align with midnight Israel time unless the server happens to match up.

Thanks for reaching out! Icons next to your name are usually status badges — things like rank, event participation, achievements, or membership tier, depending on the game. To find out exactly what yours mean, try tapping or long-pressing on the icon itself, or check your profile page — most games show a tooltip or description when you select them. If nothing pops up there, the in-game help section or FAQ under "Profile" or "Icons" should have a full list with explanations. Let us know if you still can't find info on them.

Yes, most games with display names let you change them through your account or profile settings, usually under something like "Edit Profile" or "Account Settings." Whether it costs anything (or how often you can do it for free) varies, so check the settings menu itself — it usually shows any cost or cooldown right before you confirm the change. If you don't see that option there, let us know and we can point you in the right direction.

Thanks for reaching out! The number of friends needed and any level requirement can vary depending on the specific event or referral program running at the time, so the best place to check is the Invite Friends screen or event details panel in-game — it usually lists the exact number required and any conditions (like reaching a certain level) needed for the reward to count. If it's tied to a limited-time event, double check the event hasn't ended, since that can affect whether invites still count.

Good question! Whether the game works without an internet connection depends on how it's built — some games have a true offline mode, while others need a connection to sync progress, load content, or verify things even for single-player play.

The best way to check is to look in the game's Settings or Help/FAQ menu for anything mentioning "offline mode" or "airplane mode." You can also try switching your device to airplane mode before boarding and opening the game to see what loads. If it needs login or shows a connection error, it likely requires internet to play.

Thanks for reporting this — sorry it's getting in the way of playing. You've already given us the device and OS, which helps a lot. Could you also let us know what you were doing right before the crash started happening (for example, did it crash the very first time you opened it after updating, or after playing for a bit)? Also, try a quick restart of your phone and make sure the app is fully updated from the store, as that sometimes clears up startup crashes. Let us know what you find and we'll keep digging from there.

Thanks for the details — sorry this is getting in the way of playing. Since reinstalling hasn't fixed it, it'd help to dig a bit deeper: could you let us know your device model, the operating system version it's running, and what you were doing right before the black screen showed up (e.g., launching the app fresh, resuming from background, entering a specific mode)? That'll help narrow down what's going on.

Thanks for flagging this — a frozen spin button is annoying, especially when the rest of the menu is responsive.

To help track this down, could you let us know your device model, the operating system version you're running, and what you were doing right before the button froze (e.g., just opened the app, mid-spin, after a bonus round, etc.)?

Once we have those details we can look into what might be causing it. If you're able to, a quick screen recording of the issue would also help a lot.

Thanks for reporting this - a freeze mid-raid is frustrating, especially when it kicks you back to the map. To help us dig into it, could you confirm the iOS version you're running, and let us know what you were doing right before the freeze (starting a raid, mid-battle, opening a menu, etc.)? Any detail on how consistently it happens (every raid, certain raid types only) would help too. We'll take a look once we have that info.

Thanks for reporting this - sound issues can be frustrating to troubleshoot. To help narrow down what's going on, could you let me know your device model, the operating system version you're running, and what you were doing in the game right before the sound stopped working?

In the meantime, it might be worth checking if closing the app completely and reopening it makes any difference, though I know you've already confirmed the in-game and phone settings look correct.

Thanks for flagging this — text overlapping with buttons in the shop screen definitely shouldn't happen. To help the team look into it, could you let us know your device model, the operating system version you're running, and what you were doing right before you noticed the overlap (e.g., opening the shop from the main menu, switching language settings, etc.)? A screenshot of the issue would also help a lot if you're able to share one. Thanks for your patience while we look into this.

Thanks for flagging this — a sudden slowdown like that is frustrating, especially when it was running fine before. To help track down what's going on, could you let me know your device model, the operating system version it's running, and what you were doing in the game right before things started lagging (like entering a specific mode, loading a screen, etc.)?

In the meantime, it might be worth checking if there's a pending app or OS update available, and confirming how much free storage space is on your device, since both can affect performance.

Thanks for flagging this—that's frustrating to deal with every time. To help sort out what's going on, could you let me know your device model, operating system version, and what you were doing right before the popup appeared? That'll help pin down what's causing it. In the meantime, try tapping outside the popup or using the back gesture/button, as those sometimes work even when the X isn't showing.

Thanks for flagging this—that kind of battery drain isn't normal and is worth digging into. Could you let me know your device model, the operating system version it's running, and what you were doing in the game right before you noticed the drain (e.g. a specific level, menu, or feature)? That'll help pin down what's causing it after the update.

Thanks for flagging this — losing those reminders is annoying when you're counting on them. Could you also double-check in your phone's system settings that notifications for the app are allowed (not just inside the app itself)? To help us dig into what's happening on our end, could you let me know your device model, operating system version, and what you were doing in the app right before you noticed the reminders had stopped?

Thanks for flagging this — that's frustrating when you can't read the menu to fix the menu! Language settings are usually found in the same spot regardless of the interface language, so look for a gear/cog icon (Settings), then a section often marked with a globe icon or "A/文/あ"-style icon — that's typically the language menu. It's usually near the top or bottom of the main Settings screen. If you can share a screenshot of your settings screen, we may be able to point to the exact icon even without reading the text.

Thanks for reporting this—an album crash every time is worth digging into. Could you tell us your device model, the operating system version it's running, and what you were doing right before opening the album (e.g., just launched the app, coming from a match, claiming a reward, etc.)?

That info will help narrow down what's triggering it. If you're able to try a quick fix in the meantime—like closing the app fully and reopening, or checking for a pending app update—it might be worth a shot, but the details above are the most useful thing you can send us right now.

Thanks for flagging this — a mismatched event timer is worth digging into. Could you let me know your device model, your operating system version, and what you were doing in the app right before you noticed the timer was off? That will help figure out what's going on. In the meantime, keep an eye on the in-game event screen directly, since that's the most reliable source for actual event status.

Thanks for flagging this — a 502 usually points to a server-side hiccup, but let's rule out anything on your end too. Could you tell me your device model, the operating system version you're running, and what you were doing in the app right before the error first showed up? That'll help narrow down what's going on.

Thanks for flagging this — sounds frustrating. To help track down what's going on, could you tell us your tablet's model, the operating system version it's running, and what you were doing in the game right before the screen got stuck?

In the meantime, try fully closing the app (not just backgrounding it) and reopening it, and check that your tablet's own auto-rotate setting is turned on, as some games rely on that.

Hi there — that's a rule rather than a bug. Most games with card trading restrict certain tiers (like gold/rare cards) from being traded to keep the economy balanced and prevent exploits. To check exactly which cards are restricted in your case, look at the card's details screen — it usually shows a "tradeable" or "restricted" tag, or there may be a note in the trading menu explaining which categories are excluded. If a card you believe should be tradeable is showing as locked, let us know which specific card it is so we can look into it further.

Good question — most games don't delete accounts just for inactivity, but the exact rules can vary. The best way to check is to look for an "inactivity policy" or similar section in this game's Terms of Service or FAQ/support pages — that'll tell you if there's any timeframe involved and what happens to progress, currency, or items. If you're worried about losing anything specific, it's a good idea to make sure your account is linked to an email or platform account (like Google Play, Game Center, etc.) so your progress stays recoverable either way.
